front.title: System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) Resource Types for Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers and Tool Groups

abstract.t:
AI agents reach tools through servers that implement the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Organizations decide which MCP servers are approved, who is accountable for each, who may use each, and when one must be withdrawn. Identity and governance systems make those decisions, but the gateways, private registries and agent hosts that act on them come from many vendors and have no common way to receive them.
This document defines a SCIM resource type, McpServer, that carries an organization's governance record for an MCP server: its endpoint, the OAuth protected resource identifier and authorization servers that protect it, its owners, the principals eligible to use it, an optional list of approved tools, and whether it is approved for use. It also defines McpToolGroup, a named set of tools drawn from one or more MCP servers together with the principals eligible to use them. It specifies how gateways, registries and hosts act on these records and how SCIM Security Event Tokens signal changes to them. It does not describe MCP server capabilities, which remain the subject of MCP's own metadata, and it does not authorize individual tool invocations.
